---
title: User-supplied grammar (TOML)
format: html
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      noErrors: true
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        # Container marks the block with the language class, same as
        # built-ins. Tree-sitter captures from tree-sitter-toml's own
        # highlights.scm produce `hl-string`, `hl-number`, `hl-operator`
        # spans — these map 1:1 from the capture names in the grammar's
        # query file.
        - [!str "<pre class=\"sourceCode toml\"",
           !str "hl-string\">&quot;example&quot;</span>",
           !str "hl-number\">42</span>",
           !str "hl-operator\">=</span>"]
---

Quarto picks up tree-sitter grammars that are **not** built in but
live alongside your project. Drop them under
`_quarto/grammars/<name>/` with two files:

- `<name>.wasm` — the grammar compiled with `tree-sitter build --wasm`
  (or downloaded from a release asset).
- `highlights.scm` — the tree-sitter query file that assigns capture
  names to syntactic patterns. Its classes flow through to the HTML
  output as `hl-<capture-with-dots-as-hyphens>` spans.

Optional extras (`injections.scm`, `locals.scm`) are read if present.

This document includes [tree-sitter-toml v0.7.0](https://github.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-toml)
under `_quarto/grammars/toml/`, then uses it to highlight a plain
`toml` code block:

```toml
name = "example"
count = 42
```

TOML isn't in the 14 built-in languages, but the user grammar takes
priority on class collision anyway — so you can override a built-in
the same way you'd add a new one.
